name: erdos_gyarfas
claim_latex: Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture (1995): every finite graph with minimum degree at least $3$ contains a simple cycle whose length is a power of $2$.

given_facts.statement: The conjecture holds for 3-connected cubic planar graphs.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: POSITIVE partial result for a restricted class. Says nothing about non-planar or non-cubic graphs. Concluding the full conjecture from F1 is a scope error.
given_facts.citation: C. Heckman, R. Krakovski, 'Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture for cubic planar graphs', Electron. J. Combin. 20(2) #P7 (2013). Long, partly computer-assisted discharging proof.
warns: Any counterexample must be non-planar or non-3-connected or non-cubic within the cubic planar class boundaries.

given_facts.statement: The conjecture holds for $P_{10}$-free graphs (no induced path on 10 vertices), and for $P_{13}$-free graphs with computer search.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: POSITIVE partial result. A counterexample must contain an induced $P_{10}$.
given_facts.citation: Hu, Shen, Discrete Mathematics (2024), doi 10.1016/j.disc.2024.114175; arXiv:2410.22842.
warns: Together with F1/F3 this constrains any counterexample to be long-path-rich and predominantly cubic with >= 30 vertices.

given_facts.statement: Any cubic counterexample has at least 30 vertices (Markström, computer search), and every minimal counterexample is 'predominantly cubic' (2026 preprint).
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: Constraints on a HYPOTHETICAL counterexample; they do not assert one exists. Reading F3 as evidence a counterexample exists is a sign error.
given_facts.citation: K. Markström (computer search, cubic graphs up to 29 vertices); 'Every Minimal Counterexample to the Erdős–Gyárfás Conjecture is Predominantly Cubic', arXiv:2605.22844 (May 2026).
warns: The witness search space is therefore: sparse, near-cubic, non-planar-ish graphs with >= 30 vertices and no 4-, 8-, 16-, 32-cycle. The verifier caps at 64 vertices.

witness_schema.num_vertices: int in [4, 64] — vertex count; vertices are 0-indexed
witness_schema.edges: list of [u, v] pairs, simple graph (no loops or duplicate edges), every vertex degree >= 3, at most 160 edges

note: Witness-decidable disproof target: one finite graph settles the claim. The verifier is CONSERVATIVE — it accepts only when its exhaustive per-length cycle search completes within the node-expansion budget and finds no cycle of length 4, 8, 16, 32, or 64 (whichever are <= n); budget exhaustion is a rejection. Near-cubic graphs (the only plausible witness shape per F3) are cheap to search exhaustively. Track 1-style search also fits: generate min-degree-3 graphs (e.g. girth-biased lifts, voltage graphs over Z_m, cages) and screen with the same verifier. Sanity anchors: K_4 contains a 4-cycle; the Petersen graph (girth 5) contains 8-cycles — both are correctly rejected.

ideation_lenses.name: cycle-space-matroid
ideation_lenses.description: Work in the F_2 cycle space / graphic matroid. Treat power-of-2 cycles as a distinguished subset of the cycle space; spanning-tree/cotree duality turns cycle statements into covering statements (Whitney duality, matroid union/intersection, feedback edge sets). Retro-predicts the R55 covering reframing - this lens belongs in the set from round 1.

ideation_lenses.name: discharging
ideation_lenses.description: Assign charge to vertices/edges and redistribute by local rules until a global count contradicts PO2-cycle-freeness under min degree 3. The workhorse of cubic/planar graph theory; F1 (Heckman-Krakovski, 3-connected cubic planar) sits next door to this lens.

ideation_lenses.name: covering-spaces-lifts
ideation_lenses.description: Voltage graphs, universal covers, quotients: how the PO2-cycle spectrum transforms under lifts and quotients. Upgrades the I-graph and Z_m-lift screens from enumeration to structure - which cycle lengths are forced downstairs given behavior upstairs?

ideation_lenses.name: spectral-moore
ideation_lenses.description: Trace/moment methods: closed 2^k-walk counts from eigenvalues; Moore-type bounds for graphs missing all even cycle lengths in {4,8,16,...}. Liu-Montgomery settled the dense regime via sublinear expanders (sufficiently large AVERAGE degree forces a power-of-2 cycle), so the live regime is bounded degree - ask which pieces of their robust-expansion toolkit survive at degree 3, and whether spectral structure pins the cubic case.

ideation_lenses.name: probabilistic-counting
ideation_lenses.description: Lovasz Local Lemma / entropy compression / first-moment: quantify the constraint density of avoiding every PO2 cycle length against the freedom of a min-degree-3 graph; make the R56 cotree-density heuristic (8/3 vs 16/3 edges per cycle) rigorous.

ideation_lenses.name: induction-decomposition
ideation_lenses.description: Thomassen-style induction on cubic graphs: ear decompositions, edge/vertex reductions preserving min degree 3, connectivity surgery. Find an operation under which a minimal counterexample collapses to a smaller one.

ideation_lenses.name: counterexample-first
ideation_lenses.description: Assume FALSE. A witness is near-cubic, >= 30 vertices (F3), contains an induced P10 (F2), and avoids C4/C8/C16/C32/C64 - note only power-of-2 lengths are forbidden: girth 4 is impossible but triangles are perfectly legal (girth >= 5 is a search heuristic, not a constraint). Either the constraints turn contradictory (a proof sketch) or they define a search space to hand to Track-1-style generation plus the witness verifier.
